newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico economic pact seen renewed in early Nov.
newsitem.headline: Mexico economic pact seen renewed in early Nov.

text.p: Mexico's annual economic pact between government, labour and business will likely be renewed in the first days of next month, the head of the Confederation of Industrial Chambers said Tuesday.
"It is probable that the renewal of the pact will take place in the first days of November," Victor Manuel Diaz Romero told reporters.
The industrial sector was preparing its proposals for the pact, officially known as the Alliance for Economic Recovery and unofficially as the Pacto, and would hand them in by Wednesday.
The Pacto sets minimum wage and utility rate policy in line with government economic targets for the next 12 months.

He said the industrial sector was negotiating for wage increases of about 17 percent for next year, slightly above the official inflation target of 15 percent, as well as tax reform to lower the fiscal burden on business.
"We are proposing to eliminate the tax on assets and to lower the tax on reinvestment of profits from 34 percent to 30 percent," he said, speaking after a meeting on small businesses.
Companies currently pay a tax of 1.8 percent of their total fixed assets.
-- Maria Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City newsroom 525 728-9553
